questions.question: The improved SHe-Box portal announced by Uttar Pradesh in May 2025 supports which gender at workplaces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Women**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SHe-Box** (Sexual Harassment electronic Box) is a specialized online portal designed to provide a single-window access to every **woman**, regardless of her work status, to register complaints related to **sexual harassment** at the workplace.
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Uttar Pradesh** government announced an improved version of the portal to enhance the safety and dignity of **women** across various sectors in the state.
 
• The portal serves as a centralized platform for the effective implementation of the **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013** (commonly known as the **POSH Act**). ***Hence, the option supporting women is correct.***
 
• By utilizing this digital interface, **women** in both the **organized** and **unorganized** sectors, including government and private employees, can ensure their grievances are reached to the concerned authorities without physical hurdles.
 
• The improved version launched in **Uttar Pradesh** features enhanced tracking mechanisms and real-time monitoring by the **Department of Women and Child Development** to ensure timely disposal of cases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The POSH Act, 2013:**
 
 
• The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act** was enacted in **2013** to provide protection against sexual harassment of **women** at workplaces and for the prevention and redressal of complaints.
 
• It defines "**sexual harassment**" to include unwelcome acts such as physical contact, a demand or request for sexual favors, making sexually colored remarks, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
 
 
 
• **Internal and Local Committees:**
 
 
• The **Act** mandates that any workplace with **10 or more employees** must constitute an **Internal Committee (IC)** to handle complaints.
 
• For organizations with fewer than **10 employees** or for complaints against the employer themselves, a **Local Committee (LC)** is established by the **District Officer** in every district.
 
 
 
• **Mission Shakti in Uttar Pradesh:**
 
 
• The **Uttar Pradesh** government has been integrating the **SHe-Box** portal with its flagship **Mission Shakti** program, which aims to empower **women** through **security, dignity, and self-reliance**.
 
• The state initiative focuses on establishing **Women Help Desks** in all **1,535 police stations** and ensuring that digital platforms like **SHe-Box** are accessible even at the **Gram Panchayat** level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Confidentiality and Tracking:**
 
 
• One of the primary features of the **SHe-Box** portal is the **confidentiality** it provides to the **complainant**, ensuring that her identity is not disclosed during the initial registration process.
 
• Once a complaint is lodged, both the **complainant** and the **Ministry/Department** can monitor the progress of the inquiry, which brings **transparency** and **accountability** to the **Internal Committee**.
 
 
 
• **Applicability to Unorganized Sector:**
 
 
• The portal is particularly vital for the **unorganized sector**, where **women** workers like domestic help, daily wage laborers, and street vendors often lack a formal grievance redressal mechanism.
 
• By providing a direct link to the **District Local Committees**, the **Uttar Pradesh** portal ensures that **women** at the grassroots level are not left behind in the pursuit of **justice**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: For balancing economic growth with environmental protection, the government of Uttarakhand in October 2025 launched which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nine-point policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of **Uttarakhand**, led by the state administration, officially launched the **Nine-point policy** in **October 2025** to address the dual challenges of rapid industrialization and the preservation of the **Himalayan ecology**.
 
• The primary objective of this policy is to achieve a **sustainable equilibrium** between **economic growth** and **environmental protection**, ensuring that development projects do not compromise the state's natural resources.
 
• This **Nine-point policy** focuses on key sectors such as **eco-tourism**, **renewable energy expansion**, and **sustainable agriculture**, which are vital for the state's **Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP)**.
 
• It emphasizes the **conservation of water bodies** and the management of **forest resources**, which are critical for the **fragile ecosystem** of the hill state.
 
• The policy was introduced as part of the state's vision for the **year 2025**, marking a significant milestone in its journey toward becoming a **"Green State"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uttarakhand's Environmental Context:**
 
 
• The state of **Uttarakhand** was carved out of **Uttar Pradesh** on **9 November 2000**, and its geography is dominated by the **Himalayas**, making it highly susceptible to **climate change** and **natural disasters**.
 
• In **2021**, Uttarakhand became the first state in **India** to introduce the concept of **Gross Environmental Product (GEP)**, a metric to measure the health of its natural ecosystem alongside economic data.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Vision for 2025:**
 
 
• The **year 2025** is significant as it represents the **Silver Jubilee** of the state's formation. The government has set several targets under the **"Strong Uttarakhand"** mission to double the state's **GSDP** by this time.
 
• The **Nine-point policy** serves as a framework to ensure that this **doubling of the economy** is inclusive and **environmentally resilient**.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes of the Policy:**
 
 
• The policy integrates **disaster mitigation** strategies, particularly focusing on **landslide prevention** and **flood management**, which have historically affected regions like **Kedarnath** and **Joshimath**.
 
• It also promotes **vocal for local** initiatives by supporting **organic farming** and **local handicrafts** to reduce the **carbon footprint** of logistics and transportation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Specific Characteristics of the Policy:**
 
 
• The **Nine-point policy** includes the implementation of **stringent waste management** protocols in **high-altitude trekking routes** and **pilgrimage sites** to curb **plastic pollution**.
 
• It mandates **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA)** for all new **infrastructure projects**, including **hydroelectric power plants** and **national highways**, to minimize **deforestation**.
 
• The policy encourages **community-based conservation**, where **Van Panchayats** (Forest Councils) are given more **financial autonomy** to manage **local forests**.
 
• It aligns with the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** of the **Government of India**, focusing on the **National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem**.
 
• The **Nine-point policy** is expected to generate **green jobs** for the youth of **Uttarakhand**, particularly in the **solar energy** and **eco-hospitality** sectors.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which among the following countries was visited by the Prime Minister of India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Croatia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Prime Minister of India**, **Narendra Modi**, undertook a significant state visit to **Croatia** in **June 2025** to strengthen bilateral relations and expand the strategic footprint of India in **Central and Southeast Europe**.
 
• During this visit, the Prime Minister held high-level delegation talks with the **Croatian Prime Minister**, **Andrej Plenković**, focusing on deepening cooperation in sectors such as **defense**, **digital technology**, and **renewable energy**.
 
• A series of **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** were signed, notably in the field of **Information Technology** and **Pharmaceuticals**, aiming to leverage Croatia's position as a gateway to the **European Union** markets.
 
• The visit emphasized the **India-Croatia Strategic Partnership**, with both nations agreeing to enhance **bilateral trade**, which has seen steady growth over the last decade, and to collaborate on **climate action** initiatives.
 
• The Prime Minister also engaged with the **Indian Diaspora** in **Zagreb**, acknowledging their role in fostering cultural and economic ties between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography and Location:**
 
 
• **Croatia** is a country located at the crossroads of **Central and Southeast Europe**, on the **Adriatic Sea**. It borders **Slovenia** to the northwest, **Hungary** to the northeast, **Serbia** to the east, and **Bosnia and Herzegovina** and **Montenegro** to the southeast.
 
• Its capital and largest city is **Zagreb**, which serves as the political and economic hub of the country.
 
 
 
• **Political and Economic Profile:**
 
 
• **Croatia** became a member of the **European Union (EU)** on **July 1, 2013**, and officially joined the **Schengen Area** and the **Eurozone** on **January 1, 2023**, adopting the **Euro** as its official currency.
 
• The country is a **parliamentary republic**, with the **President** serving as the head of state and the **Prime Minister** as the head of government.
 
 
 
• **Bilateral Relations with India:**
 
 
• Diplomatic relations between **India** and **Croatia** were established in **1992** following Croatia's independence from **Yugoslavia**.
 
• India and Croatia share a history of cooperation dating back to the **Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)**, where India and the former Yugoslavia were founding members.
 
• Key areas of export from India to Croatia include **textiles**, **chemicals**, and **engineering goods**, while India imports **machinery** and **plastics** from Croatia.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Culture:**
 
 
• **Croatia** is a major global tourist destination, famous for its **Dalmatian Coast** and historical sites like **Dubrovnik**, often referred to as the "Pearl of the Adriatic."
 
• The cultural exchange between the two nations is promoted through the **Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR)**, which offers scholarships to Croatian students.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The visit in **June 2025** is considered a milestone in **India's "Look West"** policy (in the context of European engagement), aiming to diversify partnerships beyond the traditional major powers of Western Europe.
 
• Discussions on the **India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA)** remained a central theme, with **Croatia** expressing strong support for the early conclusion of the negotiations to benefit small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in both regions.
 
• **Security Cooperation:** Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to **counter-terrorism** and maritime security in the **Indo-Pacific** and **Mediterranean** regions, highlighting the importance of a **rules-based international order**.

questions.question: Who among the following received the prestigious 2024 Vigyan Ratna award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Govindarajan Padmanabhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India announced the first edition of the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar** in **2024**, which are the highest national awards in the field of science, technology, and innovation.
 
• **Professor Govindarajan Padmanabhan** was selected as the recipient of the prestigious **Vigyan Ratna** award for his lifetime achievements and monumental contributions to **Biological Sciences**.
 
• He is a renowned **biochemist** and has served as the former **Director** of the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, located in **Bengaluru**.
 
• His research work is globally recognized, particularly his studies on the **molecular biology** of the **malaria parasite** and the process of **heme biosynthesis**.
 
• The award ceremony was held on **August 23, 2024**, a date celebrated as **National Space Day** to commemorate the success of the **Chandrayaan-3** mission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP) Structure**:
 
 
• The awards are organized into four distinct categories: **Vigyan Ratna**, **Vigyan Shri**, **Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar**, and **Vigyan Team**.
 
• In **2024**, a total of **33** awards were announced across these categories to honor scientists from various domains.
 
 
 
• **Vigyan Shri Awards**:
 
 
• This category recognizes distinguished contributions in science and technology. In **2024**, **13** scientists were honored, including individuals like **Anandharamakrishnan C.** and **Umesh Varshney**.
 
 
 
• **Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (SSB)**:
 
 
• This award is aimed at young scientists under the **age of 45** who have made exceptional contributions. A total of **18** researchers received this award in the inaugural year.
 
 
 
• **Vigyan Team Award**:
 
 
• This is awarded to a team of **three or more** scientists for collaborative excellence. The **ISRO-Chandrayaan 3** team was the recipient of this award in **2024** for their historic lunar landing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Vigyan Ratna** award is the top-most honor among the national science awards, reserved for **lifetime achievement**. **Govindarajan Padmanabhan** was the sole recipient of this specific category in **2024**.
 
• Selection for these awards is carried out by the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar Committee (RVPC)**, which is chaired by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the **Government of India**.
 
• The awards cover **13 domains**, including **Physics**, **Chemistry**, **Mathematics & Computer Science**, **Earth Sciences**, **Medicine**, **Engineering**, and **Agricultural Science**, among others.
 
• **Govindarajan Padmanabhan** has previously been honored with the **Padma Shri** in **1991** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2003** for his contributions to the **biotechnology** and **science** sectors in India.
 
• The institution of the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar** was part of a government initiative to streamline and bring all scientific awards under a unified, high-prestige framework.
</ul

• The narrative is set in the **11th century** and follows a group of **Chola** warriors on a high-stakes mission to reclaim the prestige of India following the raid on the **Somnath Temple** by **Mahmud of Ghazni**. 
• It highlights the legendary maritime strength of the **Chola Empire** and their commitment to protecting the cultural and religious integrity of the Indian subcontinent.

• **Natwar Singh:** 
• A former **Indian diplomat** and **politician** who served as the **Minister of External Affairs** from **2004** to **2005**. 
• He is an accomplished author, most famous for his autobiography **One Life is Not Enough**, published in **2014**. 
• His other works include **My China Diary** and **Walking with Lions: Tales from a Diplomatic Past**.

questions.question: The Indian contingent participating in the Joint Military Exercise MITRA SHAKTI-2025 is mainly represented by which regiment of the Indian Army?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajput Regiment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **10th edition** of the joint military exercise **MITRA SHAKTI** was conducted in **August 2024** (often referred to in upcoming training cycles as the 2024-25 series). The Indian Army contingent was primarily represented by a battalion of the **Rajput Regiment**.
 
• The exercise took place from **August 12 to August 25, 2024**, at the **Army Training School** located in **Maduru Oya, Sri Lanka**.
 
• The Indian contingent comprised **120 personnel**, while the **Sri Lankan Army** was represented by personnel from the **Gajaba Regiment**.
 
• The primary focus of the **MITRA SHAKTI** exercise is to enhance **interoperability** and mutual understanding between the two nations' armed forces, specifically for **counter-insurgency** and **counter-terrorism** operations.
 
• The **Rajput Regiment**, known for its bravery and long history, was chosen to lead the tactical drills, showcasing the **Indian Army's** expertise in **sub-conventional operations**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rajput Regiment.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Exercise MITRA SHAKTI:**
 
 
• This is an **annual bilateral exercise** between **India** and **Sri Lanka** that began in **2012**.
 
• It alternates between India and Sri Lanka; the **9th edition** was held in **Aundh, Pune** in **November 2023**.
 
• The exercise is conducted under the **United Nations (UN) Charter**, specifically **Chapter VII**, which deals with peace enforcement and security operations.
 
 
 
• **Scope and Drills:**
 
 
• The training involves **tactical maneuvers**, **heliborne operations**, and the integration of **Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS)** and **drones** to counter modern threats.
 
• It also includes **Combat Engineering** tasks and exercises in **semi-urban** environments to prepare troops for diverse combat scenarios.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:**
 
 
• The exercise strengthens the **bilateral defense cooperation** and the **security architecture** in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• It fosters **diplomatic ties** and professional camaraderie between the soldiers of both neighboring countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Rajput Regiment:**
 
 
• One of the oldest and most prestigious infantry regiments of the **Indian Army**, it was formally established in **1778**.
 
• The regiment has participated in several major conflicts, including both **World Wars**, the **Indo-Pak wars**, and various **UN Peacekeeping missions**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**

questions.question: Who won the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) Final held in June 2025 at Lord’s by defeating Australia by 5 wickets to claim their first WTC title?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**South Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **South Africa** made history by winning their first-ever **ICC World Test Championship (WTC)** title in **June 2025**.
 
• The final was held at the iconic **Lord's Cricket Ground** in **London**, which is widely recognized as the **"Home of Cricket"**.
 
• The **Proteas** (South Africa) achieved this feat by defeating **Australia** by a margin of **5 wickets** in a highly competitive encounter.
 
• By winning this title, **South Africa** became the third nation to lift the **WTC Mace**, following **New Zealand** (2021) and **Australia** (2023).
 
• This victory concluded the **2023-2025 WTC cycle**, where teams competed over **two years** in various bilateral series to qualify for the ultimate final.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICC World Test Championship (WTC):**
 
 
• The **WTC** was introduced by the **International Cricket Council** to add context to **Test Cricket**, ensuring that every bilateral series contributes to a global ranking.
 
• The league involves the **top nine Test-playing nations** competing in series both at home and away.
 
• The **first edition (2019-2021)** was won by **New Zealand**, who defeated **India** at **Southampton**.
 
• The **second edition (2021-2023)** saw **Australia** emerge as champions after beating **India** at **The Oval** in **London**.
 
 
 
• **Qualification Process:**
 
 
• Teams are ranked based on the **Percentage of Points (PCT)** system rather than total points to account for the varying number of matches played by different nations.
 
• The **top two teams** on the points table at the end of the league phase advance to the **one-off final** match.
 
 
 
• **Venues of WTC Finals:**
 
 
• The finals have traditionally been hosted in **England**. The venues include the **Rose Bowl** (Southampton) in **2021**, **The Oval** (London) in **2023**, and **Lord's** (London) for the **2025** edition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Australia's Performance:** **Australia** entered the **2025 final** as the defending champions but were unable to secure back-to-back titles against a resilient **South African** side.
 
• **The WTC Mace:** The winner of the final is awarded the **ICC Test Championship Mace**, symbolizing supremacy in the longest format of the game, along with a significant **prize money** component.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The **2025** win by **South Africa** highlighted the growth of their domestic structures and the effectiveness of their pace-heavy bowling attack in **English conditions**.
 
• **Match Summary:** Chasing a target in the final innings at **Lord's** is historically difficult, making **South Africa's** **5-wicket** victory a testament to their batting depth and composure under pressure.
</ul

questions.question: In IPL 2025, who became the first Indian to score 1000 runs against four IPL teams?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virat Kohli**__.

__
 
• **Virat Kohli**, playing for **Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB)**, became the **first Indian cricketer** to amass **1000 runs** against **four different teams** in the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** history by the **2025** season.
 
• The four franchises against which **Kohli** has achieved this milestone are **Delhi Capitals (DC)**, **Punjab Kings (PBKS)**, **Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR)**, and **Chennai Super Kings (CSK)**. ***Hence, the statement is correct regarding his record-breaking feat.***
 
• This achievement highlights his immense **consistency** and **longevity** in the league, where he has been a part of the same franchise since the inaugural season in **2008**.
 
• Before **Kohli**, only **David Warner** (an overseas player) had shown similar dominance against multiple teams, but **Kohli** is the **pioneer among Indian batters** to reach the quadruple 1000-run mark.
 
• During the **2024** and **2025** period, **Kohli** significantly accelerated his run-scoring, crossing the **8000-run** total mark in the **IPL**, making him the **all-time leading run-getter** in the tournament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rohit Sharma:**
 
 
• The former **Mumbai Indians** captain was the **first player** in IPL history to score **1000 runs** against a single team, which was **Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR)**.
 
• He also crossed the 1000-run mark against **Delhi Capitals (DC)**, but he currently trails **Kohli** in terms of the number of teams he has dominated to this extent.
 
 
 
• **Shikhar Dhawan:**
 
 
• Known for his prolific scoring at the top of the order, **Dhawan** has scored over **1000 runs** against **Chennai Super Kings (CSK)** and has come close against **Punjab Kings** and **Mumbai Indians**.
 
• He is the **second-highest run-scorer** in IPL history after **Virat Kohli**, with over **6700 runs** to his name across various franchises like **SRH**, **DC**, and **PBKS**.
 
 
 
• **Suresh Raina:**
 
 
• Often called **"Mr. IPL"**, **Raina** was the first player to reach the **5000-run milestone** in the league.
 
• While he was highly consistent for **Chennai Super Kings**, he retired from the **IPL** before he could complete 1000 runs against four individual opponents.
 
 
 
• **David Warner:**
 
 
• The **Australian** opening batter holds the record for the most **50+ scores** in the **IPL**.
 
• He has scored 1000+ runs against **Kolkata Knight Riders** and **Punjab Kings**, showcasing the highest level of dominance by an overseas player.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IPL Centuries Record:** **Virat Kohli** also holds the record for the **most centuries** in the **IPL**, surpassing **Chris Gayle's** long-standing record of **6 centuries**. As of **2024/25**, Kohli has recorded **8 centuries**.
 
• **Orange Cap:** **Kohli** won the **Orange Cap** in the **2016** season with a record-breaking **973 runs** and again showcased elite form in the **2024** season to win the **Orange Cap** with over **741 runs**.

</ul

questions.question: In May 2025, which Indian city mandated anti-smog guns at buildings above 3,000 square metres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Delhi** government issued a directive making it mandatory for all construction and demolition sites with a plot area of more than **3,000 square metres** to install **anti-smog guns** to control dust pollution.
 
• This mandate is part of the city's year-round effort to combat deteriorating air quality, particularly focusing on **Particulate Matter (PM 10 and PM 2.5)** generated from **Construction and Demolition (C&D)** activities.
 
• The **Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC)** is the primary body responsible for monitoring the implementation of this rule and ensuring that these devices are operational during work hours.
 
• Prior to this, the threshold for mandatory anti-smog guns was higher, but the government lowered it to **3,000 square metres** to cover a larger number of mid-sized private and public infrastructure projects.
 
• Failure to comply with these regulations leads to heavy **environmental compensation fines** and the potential **stoppage of work** under the direction of the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anti-smog Guns:**
 
 
• An **anti-smog gun** is a device that sprays **atomized water** (tiny droplets) into the air through a high-pressure propeller.
 
• The water droplets bind with **dust particles** and **suspended particulate matter**, causing them to settle on the ground, thereby clearing the air.
 
• These devices are often mounted on **trucks** or **stationary platforms** at high-vulnerability points like large excavation sites.
 
 
 
• **Dust Mitigation Guidelines:**
 
 
• Construction sites in **Delhi** are required to follow a **14-point dust mitigation** checklist, which includes covering materials with **green tarpaulin** and washing vehicle tires.
 
• Project proponents must register on the **C&D Waste Management Portal** to allow the government to monitor self-compliance through **remote sensing** and video feeds.
 
 
 
• **Air Quality Context:**
 
 
• **Delhi** frequently records **AQI (Air Quality Index)** levels in the 'Poor' to 'Severe' categories, especially during the onset of winter.
 
• The **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** is an emergency framework that kicks in depending on the severity of pollution, where **Stage I** to **Stage IV** measures are applied across the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CAQM (Commission for Air Quality Management):** This is a statutory body established for better coordination, research, and resolution of problems surrounding the air quality in the **NCR** and adjoining areas like **Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan**.
 
• **PM 10 vs PM 2.5:** **PM 10** refers to particles with a diameter of 10 micrometers or less (often dust), while **PM 2.5** refers to finer particles (often from combustion) that can penetrate deep into the lungs. **Anti-smog guns** are particularly effective against the coarser **PM 10** dust.
 
• **Regulatory Evolution:** The evolution of these rules shows a transition from voluntary compliance to **strict legal mandates**, reflecting the urgency of the environmental crisis in **North India**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organisations released the second edition of the draft of the National Essential Diagnostics List (NEDL) in January 2025?

options.text: The Indian Council of Medical Research
Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Indian Council of Medical Research**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)** released the second edition of the draft **National Essential Diagnostics List (NEDL)** in **January 2025** to enhance the diagnostic infrastructure across the country.
 
• The **NEDL** serves as a comprehensive guide for the government to prioritize the availability of **essential diagnostic tests** at various levels of healthcare, ranging from **Village-level** facilities to **Tertiary Care** centers.
 
• India became the **first country in the world** to compile and release a **National Essential Diagnostics List** when the first edition was launched in **2019**.
 
• The **2025 draft edition** includes updated lists of **in-vitro diagnostics (IVDs)**, including tests for **infectious diseases**, **non-communicable diseases (NCDs)**, and specialized tests for **maternal and child health**.
 
• The primary objective of the **ICMR** through this list is to bridge the gap between **clinical diagnosis** and treatment, ensuring that patients do not have to travel long distances for **basic diagnostic services**. ***Hence, the correct answer is The Indian Council of Medical Research.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR):**
 
 
• Established in **1911** as the **Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA)**, it was renamed **ICMR** in **1949**.
 
• It is the apex body in India for the formulation, coordination, and promotion of **biomedical research** and is funded by the **Government of India** through the **Department of Health Research**, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it oversees **27 institutes** across India focusing on specific health topics like **virology, nutrition, and oncology**.
 
 
 
• **WHO Essential Diagnostics List (EDL):**
 
 
• The **NEDL** is inspired by the **World Health Organization’s (WHO)** first **Essential Diagnostics List**, which was released in **May 2018** to provide a blueprint for countries to improve diagnostic access.
 
• While the **WHO EDL** provides a global reference, the **ICMR's NEDL** is tailored to the specific **epidemiological profile** and healthcare needs of the **Indian population**.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the List:**
 
 
• The list categorizes tests based on healthcare settings: **Level 1 (Health and Wellness Centers)**, **Level 2 (Primary Health Centers)**, **Level 3 (Community Health Centers)**, and **Level 4 (District Hospitals)**.
 
• It includes **General laboratory tests** (blood, urine, etc.) and **Disease-specific tests** (HIV, Hepatitis, Malaria, Tuberculosis, etc.).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Benefits of NEDL:**
 
 
• Standardizes diagnostic services, ensuring **quality assurance** and **cost-effectiveness** in the procurement of medical kits.
 
• Helps in reducing **out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE)** for citizens by making essential tests available at **public health facilities** for free or at subsidized rates.
 
• Promotes **evidence-based medical practice** by ensuring doctors have reliable diagnostic data before starting treatment.
 
 
 
• **Technological Inclusion in 2025:**
 
 
• The **second edition draft** emphasizes the inclusion of **Point-of-Care (PoC)** tests and **Molecular diagnostics**, which allow for rapid results in rural and remote areas.
 
• It also accounts for **emerging pathogens** and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) by including specific **sensitivity tests**.
